note: Bridge claims 'four competing scholarly identifications ... over the past century' for the Sun Stone's central face. Target article's 'four scholars, four different identities' section lists exactly four: Seler/Beyer's early-1900s Tonatiuh reading, Navarrete/Heyden's 1974 Tlaltecuhtli reading, Klein's 1976 Yohualtecuhtli reading, and Stuart's 2016 Moctezuma II portrait theory, spanning early 1900s to 2016, matching 'over the past century' and 'same surviving object'.

Bridge claims Bonampak murals yielded 'previously unreadable content for decades' as methods went 'from hand-copying to infrared photography.' Target's 'From hand-painted copies to infrared cameras' section confirms: Tejeda and Villagra traced the murals by eye 1946-1948, then Yale's Bonampak Documentation Project starting 1996 used infrared photography to 'record calligraphic lines and hieroglyphic texts that have faded past the point of being visible to the naked eye but still register under infrared light,' a roughly 50-year gap matching 'decades.'
